subject: MAP orientation: stakeholder roster + first 3-week cadence
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP orientation: stakeholder roster + first 3-week cadence

Daniel —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, I wanted to align on the mutual action plan (MAP) kickoff so Skyline and Redwood have the same expectations for the evaluation and close timeline. This note lays out: stakeholders, weekly cadence for the first three weeks, and initial success criteria we can validate during the POC.

High-level: goal is a production-readiness decision (go/no-go) by week 8. For the first three weeks we recommend tight cadence to unblock infra and data connections, exercise performance targets, and validate integration points.

Proposed stakeholders (please confirm):
- Daniel Park (Skyline) — Evaluation lead / product owner
- Maya Ruiz (Skyline) — SRE / infra contact
- Jordan Blake (Redwood) — AE, commercial lead
- Naomi Feldman (Redwood) — Solutions lead / MAP owner
- Marcus Lin (Redwood) — Solutions engineer (benchmarks & telemetry)
- Evelyn Hart (Redwood) — Customer success (post-POC go/no-go)

Cadence (weeks 1–3):
- Weekly checkpoint: 30 min, Thursdays 10:00–10:30 PT (standups to surface blockers)
- Technical deep-dive: week 1, 60 min (Marcus + Maya) to finalize network & auth
- Perf baseline run: week 2, 45 min (Marcus leads, Redwood to run 2 workloads)
- Quality review + acceptance criteria check: week 3, 60 min (Naomi to drive)

Initial acceptance criteria (examples):
- 99th percentile latency under 450ms for the 512-token test set
- End-to-end inference cost within target budget (TBD)
- No PII flow outside Skyline-managed VPC during tests
- Integration with Skyline’s calltracking + audit logs validated

Attachments: I attached a first-pass MAP spreadsheet (Skyline-MAP-v1.0.xlsx) and our evaluation checklist (redwood-eval-checklist.pdf). Links to the HubSpot record and the shared Drive are below.

Next steps: can you confirm the stakeholder list and the Thursday 10:00 PT cadence? If that works, Naomi will distribute a calendar series and the MAP doc will be the single source of truth.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear plan. Confirming stakeholders above (Maya and I will be the primary contacts). Thursday 10:00 PT is good for our team.

A couple quick asks before the week 1 deep-dive:
1) Can you add our security questions into the MAP (data residency, logging retention, access controls)?
2) We’d like to see any prior perf runs on comparable clinical workloads if available.

I see the attachments — I’ll review and flag items in Drive.

Best,
Daniel

Team —

I updated the MAP with owners and week-by-week checkpoints. Short summary of action items for the first three weeks (owners + due dates):

Week 0 (pre-kick):
- Naomi: send calendar series + MAP link — due 2026-11-23 EOD (done)
- Marcus: share perf harness README and a sample 512-token workload — due 2026-11-24
- Maya (Skyline): provide IP allowlist and preferred auth method — due 2026-11-24

Week 1: Tech deep-dive (60 min) — 2026-11-26 10:00 PT
- Marcus + Maya: confirm network & access steps, run basic smoke test — owner: Marcus; dependency: Maya
- Naomi: capture risk register entries during meeting — owner: Naomi

Week 2: Perf baseline & telemetry check — 2026-12-03 10:00 PT
- Marcus: run perf baseline, upload raw results to Drive — owner: Marcus; due: 2026-12-04
- Evelyn: verify observability hooks and SLAs in Redwood Console — owner: Evelyn; due: 2026-12-04

Week 3: Quality review & acceptance check — 2026-12-10 10:00 PT
- Naomi: facilitate QA session, log acceptance pass/fail items — owner: Naomi
- Daniel/Maya: provide sample queries that represent Skyline traffic — owner: Daniel; due: 2026-12-08

Elevations / blockers: if network or security gating items are not resolved by the week 1 meeting, we will engage Redwood Security to provide a detailed controls mapping (approx 48–72 hour SLA for evidence).

Links: MAP spreadsheet + perf snapshot (Drive link above).

Naomi Feldman
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

One ask from our legal/compliance reviewer: could you add a short row in the MAP that lists Redwood’s standard data retention and access controls so our reviewer can check off the initial items? If you can add that before the week1 meeting, that would speed review.

—Daniel
